topic.subject: physics
topic.title: Power, efficiency and energy calculations
topic.scopeBasis: TGS 2025-26 energy stores/transfers; TGS 2026-27: energy, power and efficiency
topic.overview: Power measures how quickly energy is transferred, while efficiency compares useful output with total input. The two ideas answer different questions and must not be confused.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: Power = energy transferred / time: P = E / t.
The watt (W) is one joule per second (1 W = 1 J/s).
A higher-power device transfers more energy each second; it is not automatically more efficient.
Efficiency = useful energy output / total energy input.
Percentage efficiency = useful output / total input x 100%.
Efficiency cannot exceed 1 or 100% because energy is conserved.
Input energy = useful output + dissipated outputs.
Sankey arrows conserve total width/value: input equals the sum of all output branches.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.meaning: unit of power equal to one joule per second
fraction of total input transferred usefully
energy transferred in the intended way
energy transferred in unintended, usually dissipated ways
flow diagram whose arrow widths represent energy values
total energy supplied to a system

workedExamples.prompt: A motor transfers 1,800 J in 30 s. Calculate power.
A lamp gives 18 J light from 120 J input. Calculate efficiency.

practicals.title: Compare power climbing stairs
practicals.aim: Estimate the power developed by a person climbing a fixed height.
practicals.variables: IV: person or climbing pace; DV: power; controls: vertical height/route when comparing pace; measurements: mass, height and time.
practicals.method: Measure mass and vertical height, time a safe climb, estimate energy change using mass x gravitational field strength x height, then divide by time.
practicals.expectedResult: For the same person and height, a shorter time gives greater power.
practicals.safety: Use a clear dry staircase, no running, supervision and a spotter where appropriate.
practicals.evaluation: Repeat timing, measure vertical rather than slope distance and discuss energy dissipated/body efficiency.

commonMistakes: Multiplying energy by time for power.
Writing 0.35% when the decimal efficiency is 0.35.
Assuming higher power always means higher efficiency.
examTips: Power asks how fast; efficiency asks what fraction is useful.
Check whether the answer is decimal or percent.
beforeStartingPractice: Read the key rules once, cover them, then retrieve them aloud or in writing.
Use MC first for confidence, but finish with typed, calculation, practical or explanation evidence.
After an error, study the explanation; the same concept returns later in a different format and again after 2 and 7 days.

practicals.subject: physics
practicals.title: Compare power climbing stairs
practicals.aim: Estimate the power developed by a person climbing a fixed height.
practicals.variables: IV: person or climbing pace; DV: power; controls: vertical height/route when comparing pace; measurements: mass, height and time.
practicals.method: Measure mass and vertical height, time a safe climb, estimate energy change using mass x gravitational field strength x height, then divide by time.
practicals.expectedResult: For the same person and height, a shorter time gives greater power.
practicals.safety: Use a clear dry staircase, no running, supervision and a spotter where appropriate.
practicals.evaluation: Repeat timing, measure vertical rather than slope distance and discuss energy dissipated/body efficiency.
